thesis: Weak setup, so a weak bull case. The long-term structure and business are intact. Price is above SMA50 and SMA200, revenue is growing about 39% YoY, the balance sheet is net cash with strong free cash flow, and the analyst mean target sits above the 90.87 high. Today's drop looks like an orderly post-earnings fade on light volume with no news cause and RSI near 50, not distribution. A bull can only argue for watching, not for a new long: the morning 74.9 stop is breached, the technical setup is none, and the only real path back is a hold of 73.39 plus an SMA20 reclaim on rising volume. Short interest of 13.9% adds squeeze convexity if that happens. Until then the evidence supports at most a neutral stance, and I do not contest Underweight on the stop-discipline basis.

rebuttal_to_bear: Anticipated bear points and my answers. (1) The stop is broken, so the thesis failed. Correct, and I concede it. I only argue it is not a Sell, because structure above SMA50 and SMA200 holds and today's low of 73.39 is untested as a close. (2) Growth is decelerating and valuation is rich (forward P/E 47.5, EV/EBITDA 151). Fair, but revenue is still up about 39% YoY with net cash and about 130M free cash flow, and the Q2 net income one-off does not change that. (3) Risk-off regime with ^TNX at 5.141. True, but healthcare leads the regime (XLV ret_21 +6.6%), so the sector is on the right side of the tape. (4) The CFO sale is a negative signal. It is under a trading plan, so it carries little information. Net: the bear wins on timing and stop discipline. The bull case only revives on a hold of 73.39 and an SMA20 reclaim (77.13) on rising volume. I make no claim for a new entry before then.
